title: Nepal's tiger population climbs to 429, nearly quadrupling since 2010 - The Himalayan Times
description: Nepal's tiger population climbs to 429, nearly quadrupling since 2010  The Himalayan Times
publisher.title: The Himalayan Times
full_article:
Key Takeaways:

Nepal's tiger population rose from 355 in 2022 to 429 in 2026, nearly quadruple the 2010 figure

Chitwan (145) and Bardiya (112) lead habitats, though Bardiya saw a decline from 125

Growth hailed as a collective conservation achievement, driven by anti-poaching and community stewardship

Rising numbers exceed habitat capacity (~400), intensifying human-tiger conflict and coexistence challenges

Nepal's wild tiger population has climbed to an estimated 429, up from 355 in 2022 and nearly four times the 121 recorded in 2010, the government announced on Wednesday as the country marked the 17th Global Tiger Day.

Related Articles TVS launches upgraded Apache RTR 160 4V in Nepal at Rs 429,900 Govt eyes 52-hectare 'Tiger Sanctuary' in Chitwan for problem tigers

The Ministry of Forests and Environment unveiled the findings of the National Tiger and Prey Base Survey 2026 in Kathmandu. The survey, conducted between December 2025 and July 2026 by the Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation and the Department of Forests and Soil Conservation, was supported by NTNC, WWF Nepal and ZSL Nepal.

Chitwan National Park recorded the highest tiger population with 145, followed by Bardiya (112), Parsa (71), Banke (51) and Shuklaphanta (50). All five parks registered increases from the 2022 census, except Bardiya, whose population declined from 125 to 112.

Researchers deployed around 1,100 camera traps across the Chitwan-Parsa, Banke-Bardiya and Shuklaphanta-Laljhadi landscapes, with about 250 personnel conducting systematic surveys and photographing tigers for at least 15 nights in each grid before analysing the images.

Worldwide, the wild tiger population has increased from about 3,200 in 2010 to 5,357 in 2025. India remains home to the largest population with 3,167 tigers, followed by Russia (750), Indonesia (400) and Nepal, whose latest census now places it ahead of Indonesia.

WWF Nepal Country Representative Dr Ghana Shyam Gurung hailed the rise as a "collective conservation achievement," crediting government leadership, community stewardship and collaboration across conservation partners.

Conservationists cautioned that Nepal's forests are estimated to have a carrying capacity of around 400 tigers, meaning the latest population exceeds the habitat's sustainable limit.

The increase has intensified concerns over human-tiger conflict, habitat fragmentation and poaching risks. Nepal currently has 16 "problem tigers"-animals involved in attacks, found injured or rescued from settlements-being housed in enclosures in Chitwan, Bardiya, Banke and the Central Zoo in Jawalakhel.

To address the growing challenge, the government has proposed a 52-hectare Tiger Sanctuary in Devnagar, Chitwan, to rehabilitate injured and conflict-affected tigers while promoting eco-tourism.

WWF Nepal said future efforts will focus on strengthening community forest user groups, buffer zone committees and local governments to improve coexistence.

The organisation also plans to expand community-based monitoring, strengthen early warning systems and rapid response mechanisms, engage more young people in conservation, and mobilise greater private-sector investment.

title: Nepal's tiger population hits record 429, but deadly conflict with humans grows - Everest Chronicle
description: Nepal's tiger population hits record 429, but deadly conflict with humans grows  Everest Chronicle
publisher.title: Everest Chronicle
full_article:
Nepal's endangered Bengal tiger population has risen to a record 429, the government announced Wednesday, marking another conservation milestone for the country even as a rise in deadly encounters between humans and big cats threatens to undermine public support for wildlife protection.

The latest National Tiger and Prey Base Survey estimated 429 wild Bengal tigers across Nepal's five protected lowland landscapes, up from 355 recorded in the previous census in 2022 -- an increase of 74 animals, or about 21 percent.

The census results, released on Global Tiger Day by the Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation, cement Nepal's status as one of the world's leading tiger conservation success stories after the country became the first tiger-range nation to almost triple its wild tiger population from 2009 levels, years ahead of the global TX2 target.

Chitwan National Park remained Nepal's most important tiger stronghold with 145 animals, up from 128 in the previous survey. Bardiya National Park had the second-largest population with 112 tigers, despite being the only protected area to record a decline, down from 125.

Parsa National Park recorded the sharpest increase, with tiger numbers rising to 71 from 41, while Banke National Park doubled its population to 51 from 25. Shuklaphanta National Park also saw an increase to 50 tigers from 36.

The nationwide survey was conducted between late December and April using thousands of camera traps across more than 7,300 square kilometres of tiger habitat. Researchers identified 363 individual tigers through stripe-pattern analysis before estimating the total population using internationally recognised statistical methods.

Officials attributed the recovery to decades of habitat protection, anti-poaching patrols, prey management and efforts to maintain wildlife corridors linking protected areas.

"Nepal's tiger population has continued to recover," conservation group WWF Nepal said in a statement, describing the increase as "another important milestone" while stressing that future conservation would depend on ensuring people and wildlife can coexist.

The success, however, has brought new challenges for communities living along the edges of protected forests.

At least 10 people have been killed in attacks by tigers over the past year, according to locals and conservation officials, with seven of the deaths reported in Bardiya district alone.

Forest officials say increasing tiger numbers have also displaced leopards from core habitats into buffer zones and villages, where they more frequently prey on livestock and occasionally attack people.

Nepal provides compensation of one million rupees to families of people killed in wildlife attacks and covers medical expenses for those injured.

Local residents and conservationists say preventing conflict will be critical to sustaining public support for the country's internationally acclaimed tiger recovery.

title: Nepal's tiger population climbs to 429 in latest national census - The Star
description: Nepal's tiger population climbs to 429 in latest national census  The Star
publisher.title: The Star
full_article:
CHITWAN: Nepal's population of the endangered Bengal tiger has increased to 429, according to the latest national tiger census released on Wednesday to mark Global Tiger Day.

The Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation unveiled the census results in Kathmandu in the presence of Minister for Agriculture, Forests and Environment Geeta Chaudhary.

Haribhadra Acharya, information officer at the department, said tiger numbers had increased in all national parks except Bardiya.

The biggest rise was recorded in Parsa National Park, where the tiger population increased to 71 from 41 in the 2022 census.

In Banke National Park, the number rose to 51 from 25, while Shuklaphanta National Park recorded an increase from 36 to 50.

Bardiya National Park, however, saw a decline, with tiger numbers falling to 112 from 125 in the previous census.

The census was conducted using camera traps between Dec 31 and April 23.

The latest count found 145 tigers in Chitwan National Park and surrounding areas, up from 128 in the previous survey.

Chitwan has seen major fluctuations in tiger numbers over the past two decades.

Around 2000, the park and surrounding forest areas had an estimated 60 tigers.

The number increased to 91 in the 2009 survey and reached 120 in 2013.

However, the 2018 census recorded a decline, with the population dropping to 93.

Following Chitwan, Bardiya has the second-highest tiger population in Nepal with 112 tigers, despite the recent decline.

Nepal recorded 355 tigers in the previous national census.

The latest figure represents an increase of 74 tigers compared with the 2022 count. - Kathmandu Post/ANN

Key Takeaways:

Gusthal Mahavihar and Agam restored in Patan with Rs 120m Indian grant

Project implemented by DUDBC with design consultancy from INTACH

Leaders hailed restoration as symbol of Nepal–India cultural ties

India has supported 30 heritage sites, plus housing, schools and health facilities under reconstruction aid

India and Nepal on Tuesday jointly inaugurated the restored Gusthal Mahavihar and Agam of Prathamshree Mahavihar in Guita Tole, Patan, a cultural heritage project rebuilt under India's post-earthquake reconstruction assistance.

Related Articles In Pictures: New Road and Durbar Marg light up with vintage street lamps Kathmandu Kalinga Literary Festival to spotlight South Asian identity, India-Nepal ties

The inauguration was jointly performed by Member of Parliament Jagdish Kharel, Lalitpur Metropolitan City Mayor Chiribabu Maharjan, and Indian Ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava. Officials from the Government of Nepal's Department of Urban Development and Building Construction (DUDBC), representatives of the local community, and the Embassy of India also attended the ceremony.

The restoration was carried out with an Indian grant of approximately Rs 120 million (NPR 12 crore) under India's post-earthquake reconstruction programme. The project was implemented by the Central Level Project Implementation Unit (Building and Housing) under the DUDBC, while the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH) provided design and project management consultancy services.

full_article: Kathmandu. Janata Samajwadi Party (JSP) Nepal has called a meeting of its central committee today. The JSP Nepal has called a meeting of its old central committee. It has been 6 months since the merger with Lospa Nepal. However, as the merger has not been finalized, both parties have started holding separate meetings. On August 3, the old executive committee of JSP Nepal held a meeting, and the executive committee of Lospa Nepal has also held a meeting. Today, the central committee meeting of JSP Nepal is being held. JSP Nepal's office secretary Pesal Dhakal said that the central committee meeting has been called to discuss the issue of unification. This meeting has been called to discuss the unification process and adjustments with Lospa Nepal within the party. He said that adjustments and other issues will be decided by this meeting. JSP Nepal has a 241-member central committee including 18 office bearers. The decision on who will be included in the unified central committee and on what criteria will be made by this meeting. A 251-member central committee has been proposed for the unified party JSP Nepal. There will be 19 office bearers in that central committee. An internal agreement has been reached between Lospa and JSP Nepal to adjust the party on a 60-40 basis. It is said that 60 percent of the leaders in the central committee of the unified party will be from JSP Nepal and 40 percent from Lospa. The executive committee meeting of Lospa Nepal held yesterday has set various criteria for adjustment with JSP Nepal. Former General Secretary of Lospa Nepal, Dr. Surendra Jha, said that leaders will be selected based on criteria such as struggle and contribution to the party, accountability to the party in elections, personality development, and youth representation. Lospa Nepal has a 307-member central committee including 65 office bearers. Since there is an internal agreement to adjust the party on a 60-40 basis between the two parties, it is necessary to select names of at most 100 people from the 307 members and send them to the central committee of the unified JSP Nepal. Therefore, it seems difficult for Lospa to select only 100 people.

title: Nepal Achieves Historic Success in Tiger Conservation, Population Rises to 429 - Ratopati
description: Nepal Achieves Historic Success in Tiger Conservation, Population Rises to 429  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Nepal has achieved another historic success in tiger conservation. According to the latest national tiger census released on Wednesday, the occasion of World Tiger Day, the number of wild Bengal tigers in Nepal has increased to 429. In the census conducted four years ago, 355 tigers were found. This time, 74 more tigers have been added, re-establishing Nepal as one of the countries successfully conserving tigers globally.

However, according to conservationists, merely increasing the number of 'striped saints' is not enough; the biggest challenge is to protect the wildlife corridors (corridors) where tigers can roam safely. As the tiger population increases within protected forest areas, they have to venture out in search of new territories. If the passage between forest areas is broken, the risk of human-tiger conflict, internal accidents, and reduced genetic diversity increases.

According to the census released by the Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation in the presence of Minister of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, Gita Chaudhary, the tiger population has increased in all major protected areas except Bardia. According to the department's information officer, Haribhadra Acharya, the biggest increase has been seen in Parsa National Park, where the tiger population has increased from 41 to 71. Banke has increased from 25 to 51, and Shuklaphanta from 36 to 50. 145 tigers have been recorded in Chitwan National Park and its surrounding areas, which is 17 more than the previous census's 128. However, in Bardia National Park, the tiger population has decreased from 125 to 112.

This census was conducted using the camera trap technique from December 31 to April 23. In the past two decades, the tiger population in Chitwan has shown fluctuations. The estimated number, which was around 60 in 2000, reached 120 in 2013, and then decreased to 93 in 2018. It has now increased again to 145.

New Challenges Begin with Increasing Numbers

Tigers are highly territorial animals. Once adult, they need to find their own territory. A male tiger can control an area of up to 200 square kilometers depending on prey availability and habitat. Young tigers, after separating from their mothers, travel long distances in search of new territories. This is why corridors are considered crucial in tiger conservation.

If the connection between forest areas is broken, tigers become confined to isolated groups. This leads to a risk of interrupted genetic exchange, increased inbreeding, and intensified competition among tigers. On the other hand, tigers venturing into human settlements in search of new territories can fall victim to accidents, poaching, or human-tiger conflict.

India's Experience: The Growing Importance of Corridors with Increasing Numbers

India, which borders Nepal, is currently facing this very challenge. In India, with a population of over 1.4 billion, the number of tigers has also increased significantly in the last decade with rapid economic growth and infrastructure expansion. The tiger population, which was around 1,827 in 1972, reached 3,682 in 2022. Currently, about 75 percent of the world's wild tigers are in India.

However, as the tiger population increases, the existing protected areas are becoming insufficient. Corridors connecting forest areas for tigers venturing out in search of new habitats have now become the most important issue in conservation. India's National Tiger Conservation Authority has identified four very important tiger landscapes and prioritized the conservation of corridors connecting them. Through these routes, tigers get opportunities to find prey, water, occupy new territories, and maintain genetic diversity among different groups.

Bilal Habib, a scientist at India's Wildlife Institute (WII), says, 'There are hardly any other developing countries in the world that invest so much in wildlife conservation.' According to him, India has already constructed 10 of the world's largest wildlife underpasses and overpasses since 2017.

Terai Arc: The Lifeline Connecting Nepal and India

The Terai Arc Landscape, connecting Nepal and India, is now considered one of the most successful tiger conservation areas in the world. Spreading across the foothills of the Himalayas, this area of about 51,000 square kilometers has 19 major wildlife corridors. According to experts, at least 10 of them are in urgent need of conservation.

In India's Rajaji Tiger Reserve, even small and narrow wildlife passages between deep canals, highways, railways, and settlements provide safe passage for tigers, elephants, and other animals. Such corridors act as lifelines connecting fragmented forest areas.

Central India: Growing Pressure Alongside Successful Conservation

The most notable example of tiger conservation success in India is considered to be Central India. The vast forest area here is now being confined to fragmented jungles. However, natural corridors connecting the remaining forest areas still provide tigers with opportunities to reach new habitats. About 40 percent of India's estimated 3,682 wild tigers reside in this region, further increasing its conservation importance. However, the gradual decline of forest areas has become the biggest concern in this region.

A study covering Panna, Pench, Bandhavgarh, Sanjay-Dubri, Achanakmar, and Indravati Tiger Reserves showed a nearly five percent decrease in forest area between 2005 and 2015. During this period, agricultural land and human settlements have expanded. The Kanha-Pench corridor, connecting Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, is now considered India's most important tiger route. According to the latest census, Kanha has 105 tigers and Pench has 77, while evidence of tigers regularly moving and even breeding has been found in the Balaghat forest area connecting these two reserves.

Accidents, Conflicts, and Development Pressure

Human-tiger conflict has also increased with the rise in tiger numbers. In Maharashtra's Chandrapur district, 150 people have died due to tiger attacks from 2021 to May 2025. In the last three years, at least 19 tigers have been killed by train collisions alone.

Similarly, mining, roads, railways, and river-linking projects are also fragmenting habitats. The proposed Ken-Betwa river-linking project within Panna Tiger Reserve alone is estimated to submerge about 57 square kilometers of forest area and displace more than two thousand families. Conservationists consider this one of India's most controversial conservation-development disputes.

'Not Just Corridors, Core Habitats Must Also Be Protected'

According to world-renowned tiger expert Ullas Karanth, constructing underpasses and overpasses alone is not a sufficient solution. He said, 'Core habitats must be protected first. No animal will use an underpass or overpass unless there is good forest on the other side.'

According to Karanth, there is still about 400,000 square kilometers of potential tiger habitat in India. 'If these habitats can be effectively conserved, India can support even 10,000 to 20,000 tigers,' he says.

Wildlife biologist Ravi Chellam also believes that corridors alone should not be considered the solution. 'Simply drawing narrow areas on a map and declaring them corridors is not a solution. Animals use the entire landscape,' he states.

Nepal has presented a successful example of conservation to the world by increasing the tiger population. But the challenge now is not to count tigers, but to create an environment where they can live safely. Protecting the wildlife corridors between Chitwan, Parsa, Banke, Bardia, and Shuklaphanta, making wildlife underpasses and overpasses mandatory on the East-West Highway, railways, and other infrastructure, and adopting a joint conservation strategy in the Nepal-India border area are the needs of the hour.

Tigers Are Returning, But Forests Are Shrinking

As conservation efforts succeed, tigers are reappearing in areas where they had previously disappeared. The sighting of a tiger at an altitude of about 2,100 meters in the Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary in the Indian Himalayas in 2023 is an example of this. In reality, these tigers have not gone to new places; they are returning to their historical habitats. According to naturalist E.P. Gee, there were about one lakh tigers across India in the early 20th century. Since then, many of those areas have been occupied by human settlements, agriculture, and infrastructure development.

The intensity of human population pressure is exemplified by the Bandhavgarh-Sanjay Dubri region. In 1901, only nine people per square kilometer lived in this area, while now 223 people reside there. In such a situation, it is natural for encounters and conflicts between tigers and humans to increase.

Tigers have the ability to travel very long distances. In January 2024, a tiger reached agricultural land near the Delhi metropolitan area, about 125 kilometers away from Sariska Tiger Reserve in Rajasthan. Although two people were injured during the journey, forest officials did not intervene as radio collar data confirmed its destination was back towards Sariska. According to experts, such incidents are likely to increase in the future.

Road Development and Conservation Hand in Hand

Roads that fragment forest areas can also become tools for wildlife conservation if planned correctly. According to Bilal Habib, a scientist at India's Wildlife Institute, road construction cannot be stopped, but it can be made wildlife-friendly. He said, 'We are not just building roads; we are restoring landscape and ecological connectivity. We are returning the land to nature.'

According to him, various Indian states have started increasing coordination, keeping in mind the cross-border movement of tigers and elephants. Efforts are being made to make the construction of underpasses, overpasses, and safe corridors for wildlife an integral part of development plans.

World-renowned tiger expert Ullas Karanth also emphasizes this point. In his words, 'Core habitats must be protected first. If habitats are conserved well, India can support even 10,000 to 20,000 tigers.' According to him, underpasses and overpasses alone are not sufficient. Tigers will use them only if there is quality forest on both sides of these structures.

This experience is also highly relevant for Nepal. As the tiger population increases in Chitwan, Parsa, Bardia, Banke, and Shuklaphanta, the challenge is no longer to increase tiger counts, but to protect the biological corridors where they can roam safely. Only by mandatorily including wildlife underpasses, overpasses, and green corridors in the East-West Highway, proposed railway, and other infrastructure projects can Nepal sustain its conservation success in the long term.

The Lesson for Nepal Now

Nepal has presented a successful example of conservation to the world by increasing the tiger population. But the challenge now is not to count tigers, but to create an environment where they can live safely. Protecting the wildlife corridors between Chitwan, Parsa, Banke, Bardia, and Shuklaphanta, making wildlife underpasses and overpasses mandatory on the East-West Highway, railways, and other infrastructure, and adopting a joint conservation strategy in the Nepal-India border area are the needs of the hour.

Indeed, the result of the increase in Nepal's tiger population is not entirely positive. According to government records, 44 people died due to tiger attacks in Nepal from 2019 to 2024. In the fiscal year 2080/81, the latest official data from the government, six people were killed and eight seriously injured by tigers. 15 tigers involved in these attacks have been captured and kept in temporary rescue and holding centers. Among them, five tigers are kept in Bardia, four in Chitwan, four in the Central Zoo in Kathmandu, and one each in Parsa and Shuklaphanta.

The increase in tiger numbers is a conservation success. However, if the forests and safe passages where they can roam freely are not protected, that success may not be long-term. This is why it is now necessary to protect not only the tigers but also the paths they walk, and to keep the communities marginalized by tigers safe. These challenges are not easy.

नेपाल बाघ संरक्षण मे एकटा आओर ऐतिहासिक सफलता प्राप्त केलक अछि । विश्व बाघ दिवस के अवसर पर बुधदिन जारी ताजा राष्ट्रीय बाघ जनगणना के अनुसार नेपाल में जंगली बंगाल बाघ के संख्या बढ़ि क 429 भ गेल अछि।चारि साल पहिने भेल जनगणना में 355 टा बाघ भेटल अछि। एहि बेर 74 टा बाघ आओर जोड़ल गेल अछि, जाहि सं नेपाल के वैश्विक स्तर पर बाघ के सफलतापूर्वक संरक्षण करय वाला देश मे सं एक के रूप मे फेर सं स्थापित कएल गेल अछि.

मुदा, संरक्षणवादी लोकनिक अनुसार, मात्र ‘पट्टीदार संत’क संख्या बढ़ेनाय पर्याप्त नहिं ; सब सं पैघ चुनौती वन्यजीवक कें गलियारा (गलियारा) कें सुरक्षा करनाय छै जत बाघ सुरक्षित रूप सं घूम सकय छै. जेना-जेना संरक्षित वन क्षेत्रक भीतर बाघक आबादी बढ़ैत जाइत अछि, ओकरा नव क्षेत्रक खोज मे उद्यम करय पड़ैत छैक । यदि वन क्षेत्रक कें बीच कें मार्ग टूट जायत छै त मानव-बाघ संघर्ष, आंतरिक दुर्घटना, आ आनुवंशिक विविधता मे कमी कें खतरा बढ़ी जायत छै.

राष्ट्रीय उद्यान एवं वन्यजीव संरक्षण विभाग द्वारा कृषि, वन एवं पर्यावरण मंत्री गीता चौधरी के उपस्थिति में जारी जनगणना के अनुसार बर्दिया के अलावा सब प्रमुख संरक्षित क्षेत्र में बाघ के आबादी बढ़ी गेलऽ छै । विभाग के सूचना अधिकारी हरिभद्र आचार्य के अनुसार सबस बेसी बढ़ोत्तरी पर्सा राष्ट्रीय उद्यान में देखल गेल अछि, जतय बाघ के आबादी 41 स बढ़ि क 71 भ गेल अछि।बांके में 25 स बढ़ि क 51, आ शुक्लफंटा में 36 स बढ़ि क 50 भ गेल अछि।चितवन राष्ट्रीय उद्यान आ ओकर आसपास के इलाका में 145 बाघ दर्ज भेल अछि, जे पहिने स 17 बेसी अछि जनगणना के 128. मुदा बर्दिया नेशनल पार्क में बाघ के आबादी 125 सं घटि क 112 भ गेल अछि.

ई जनगणना 31 दिसंबर स 23 अप्रैल तक कैमरा ट्रैप तकनीक क उपयोग कए कैल गेल छल।पिछला दू दशक मे चितवन मे बाघ क आबादी मे उतार-चढ़ाव देखबा मे आयल अछि। अनुमानित संख्या जे 2000 मे 60 क आसपास छल, 2013 मे 120 भ गेल, आ फेर 2018 मे घटि कए 93 भ गेल।आब इ फेर स बढ़ि कए 145 भ गेल अछि।

नव चुनौती बढ़ैत संख्या स शुरू होइत अछि

बाघ अत्यधिक क्षेत्रीय जानवर अछि । एक बेर वयस्क भ गेलाक बाद हुनका अपन इलाका तकबाक जरूरत अछि। नर बाघ शिकार के उपलब्धता आ आवास के आधार पर 200 वर्ग किलोमीटर तक के क्षेत्रफल पर नियंत्रण क सकैत अछि । बाघ केरऽ बच्चा, अपनऽ माय स॑ अलग होय के बाद, नया-नया इलाका के खोज म॑ बहुत दूर तक जाय छै । यही कारण छै कि बाघ संरक्षण म॑ गलियारा क॑ बहुत महत्वपूर्ण मानलऽ जाय छै ।

यदि वन क्षेत्रक बीचक संबंध टूटि जाइत अछि त बाघ अलग-थलग समूह मे सीमित भ जाइत अछि । एहि सं आनुवंशिक आदान-प्रदान मे बाधा, अंतःप्रजनन मे वृद्धि, आ बाघक बीच प्रतिस्पर्धा तेज होयबाक खतरा होइत अछि । दोसरऽ तरफ नया इलाका के खोज म॑ मानव बस्ती म॑ उतरै वाला बाघ दुर्घटना, शिकार या मानव-बाघ संघर्ष के शिकार होय सकै छै ।

भारत केरऽ अनुभव : बढ़तऽ संख्या के साथ गलियारा केरऽ बढ़तऽ महत्व

नेपाल के सीमा स सटल भारत के सामने एखन इएह चुनौती अछि। 1.4 अरब स॑ भी अधिक आबादी वाला भारत म॑ भी पिछला एक दशक म॑ तेजी स॑ आर्थिक विकास आरू बुनियादी ढांचा के विस्तार के साथ बाघऽ के संख्या म॑ काफी वृद्धि होय गेलऽ छै । बाघ के आबादी जे 1972 में लगभग 1,827 छल, 2022 में 3,682 भ गेल छल.अखन दुनिया के लगभग 75 प्रतिशत जंगली बाघ भारत में अछि.

मुदा, जेना-जेना बाघक आबादी बढ़ैत गेल अछि, मौजूदा संरक्षित क्षेत्र अपर्याप्त भ रहल अछि। नया आवास के खोज म॑ निकलै वाला बाघऽ लेली वन क्षेत्रऽ क॑ जोड़ै वाला गलियारा अब॑ संरक्षण म॑ सबसें महत्वपूर्ण मुद्दा बनी गेलऽ छै । भारत केरऽ राष्ट्रीय बाघ संरक्षण प्राधिकरण न॑ चार बहुत महत्वपूर्ण बाघ परिदृश्य के पहचान करी क॑ ओकरा जोड़ै वाला गलियारा के संरक्षण क॑ प्राथमिकता देल॑ छै । ई मार्गऽ के माध्यम स॑ बाघऽ क॑ शिकार खोजै के अवसर मिलै छै, पानी मिलै छै, नया इलाका प॑ कब्जा करै के मौका मिलै छै, आरू अलग-अलग समूहऽ के बीच आनुवंशिक विविधता क॑ कायम रखै के मौका मिलै छै ।

भारत केरऽ वन्यजीव संस्थान (WII) केरऽ वैज्ञानिक बिलाल हबीब के कहना छै कि 'दुनिया म॑ शायद ही कोनो अन्य विकासशील देश ऐन्हऽ होतै जे वन्यजीव संरक्षण म॑ एतना निवेश करै छै ।' हुनकऽ अनुसार भारत २०१७ के बाद स॑ दुनिया केरऽ १० सबसें बड़ऽ वन्यजीव अंडरपास आरू ओवरपास के निर्माण करी चुकलऽ छै ।

तराई चाप : नेपाल एवं भारत को जोड़ने वाली जीवन रेखा

नेपाल आरू भारत क॑ जोड़ै वाला तराई आर्क लैंडस्केप क॑ अब॑ दुनिया केरऽ सबसें सफल बाघ संरक्षण क्षेत्रऽ म॑ स॑ एक मानलऽ जाय छै । हिमालय केरऽ तलहटी म॑ फैललऽ लगभग ५१,००० वर्ग किलोमीटर केरऽ ई क्षेत्र म॑ १९ प्रमुख वन्यजीव गलियारा छै । विशेषज्ञ क अनुसार एहि मे स कम स कम 10टा कए संरक्षण क तत्काल जरूरत अछि।

भारत केरऽ राजाजी टाइगर रिजर्व म॑ गहरी नहर, राजमार्ग, रेलवे, आरू बस्ती के बीच छोटऽ-छोटऽ वन्यजीवऽ के रास्ता भी बाघ, हाथी आरू अन्य जानवरऽ लेली सुरक्षित रास्ता उपलब्ध करै छै । ऐहन गलियारा खंडित वन क्षेत्रक कें जोड़य वाला जीवन रेखा कें काज करएयत छै.

मध्य भारत : सफल संरक्षण के साथ-साथ बढ़ते दबाव |

भारत मे बाघ संरक्षण सफलताक सबसँ उल्लेखनीय उदाहरण मध्य भारत मानल जाइत अछि । एहि ठामक विशाल जंगल क्षेत्र आब खंडित जंगल मे सीमित भ रहल अछि। लेकिन शेष वन क्षेत्रऽ क॑ जोड़ै वाला प्राकृतिक गलियारा स॑ अखनी भी बाघऽ क॑ नया आवास प॑ पहुँचै के अवसर मिलै छै । भारत केरऽ अनुमानित ३,६८२ जंगली बाघऽ म॑ स॑ लगभग ४० प्रतिशत ई क्षेत्र म॑ निवास करै छै, जेकरा स॑ एकरऽ संरक्षण केरऽ महत्व आरू बढ़ी जाय छै । मुदा वन क्षेत्र मे धीरे-धीरे गिरावट एहि क्षेत्र मे सबस पैघ चिंता क विषय बनि गेल अछि।

पन्ना, पेंच, बंधवगढ़, संजय-दुबरी, आचनमार, आरू इंद्रवती टाइगर रिजर्व क॑ शामिल करलऽ गेलऽ एगो अध्ययन म॑ २००५ स॑ २०१५ के बीच वन क्षेत्र म॑ लगभग पांच प्रतिशत के कमी देखलऽ गेलऽ छै ।ई दौरान कृषि भूमि आरू मानव बस्ती के विस्तार होय गेलऽ छै । मध्य प्रदेश आरू महाराष्ट्र क॑ जोड़ै वाला कान्हा-पेंच गलियारा क॑ अब॑ भारत केरऽ सबस॑ महत्वपूर्ण बाघ मार्ग मानलऽ जाय छै । ताजा जनगणना के अनुसार कान्हा में 105 बाघ आ पेंच में 77 बाघ अछि, जखन कि बाघ के नियमित रूप स आवागमन आ प्रजनन तक के प्रमाण एहि दुनु रिजर्व के जोड़य वाला बालाघाट वन क्षेत्र में भेटल अछि।

दुर्घटना, संघर्ष, एवं विकास के दबाव

बाघ के संख्या बढ़ला सं मानव-बाघ के द्वंद्व सेहो बढ़ल अछि. महाराष्ट्र के चंद्रपुर जिला में 2021 स मई 2025 तक बाघ के हमला के कारण 150 लोक के मौत भ चुकल अछि।पिछला तीन साल में असगर ट्रेन के टक्कर स कम स कम 19 टा बाघ के मौत भ चुकल अछि।

तहिना खनन, सड़क, रेलवे, आ नदी सं जोड़य वाला परियोजना सेहो आवास के खंडित क रहल अछि. असगरे पन्ना टाइगर रिजर्व के भीतर प्रस्तावित केन-बेतवा नदी जोड़ै वाला परियोजना स॑ लगभग ५७ वर्ग किलोमीटर के वन क्षेत्र डूबी जाय के अनुमान छै आरू दू हजार स॑ भी अधिक परिवारऽ क॑ विस्थापित करी देलऽ जैतै । संरक्षणवादी एकरा भारत केरऽ सबसें विवादित संरक्षण-विकास विवादऽ म॑ स॑ एक मान॑ छै ।

'केवल गलियारा नहि, कोर आवास के सेहो सुरक्षा होबाक चाही'.

विश्व प्रसिद्ध बाघ विशेषज्ञ उल्लास करंथ के अनुसार असगर अंडरपास आ ओवरपास के निर्माण कोनो पर्याप्त समाधान नै अछि। ओ कहलनि जे, पहिने कोर आवास के रक्षा करय पड़त। जाबे तक दोसर कात नीक जंगल नै रहत ताबे तक कोनो जानवर अंडरपास या ओवरपास के उपयोग नै करत।'

करांत के अनुसार भारत में अखनी भी लगभग चार लाख वर्ग किलोमीटर के संभावित बाघ के आवास छै । ओ कहैत छथि जे अगर एहि आवास कए प्रभावी ढंग स संरक्षित कैल जा सकैत अछि त भारत 10 स 20 हजार बाघ कए सेहो सहारा द सकैत अछि।

वन्यजीव जीवविज्ञानी रवि चेल्लम केरऽ भी मानना ​​छै कि केवल गलियारा क॑ ही एकरऽ समाधान नै मानलऽ जाय । 'मात्र नक्शा पर संकीर्ण इलाका के चित्र बना क' ओकरा गलियारा घोषित करब कोनो समाधान नहिं.' जानवर पूरा परिदृश्य के उपयोग करै छै,' हुनकऽ कहना छै ।

नेपाल बाघक जनसंख्या बढबैत संरक्षणक सफल उदाहरण विश्वक समक्ष प्रस्तुत केलक अछि । मुदा आब चुनौती बाघ के गिनती नहिं, बल्कि एहन माहौल बनाबय के अछि जतय ओ सुरक्षित रहय. चितवन, पर्सा, बाँके, बर्दिया, आ शुक्लफंटा के बीच वन्यजीव गलियारा के सुरक्षा, पूर्व-पश्चिम राजमार्ग, रेलवे, आ अन्य बुनियादी ढांचा पर वन्यजीव के अंडरपास आ ओवरपास अनिवार्य करब, आ नेपाल-भारत सीमा क्षेत्र में संयुक्त संरक्षण रणनीति अपनाबय के काज समय के जरूरत अछि.

बाघ घुरि रहल अछि, मुदा जंगल सिकुड़ि रहल अछि

जेना-जेना संरक्षण के प्रयास सफल भ रहल अछि, बाघ ओहि इलाका मे फेर सं देखा रहल अछि जतय ओ पहिने गायब भ गेल छल. भारतीय हिमालय केरऽ बिनसर वन्यजीव अभयारण्य म॑ २०२३ म॑ लगभग २१०० मीटर के ऊंचाई प॑ बाघ केरऽ दर्शन एकरऽ उदाहरण छेकै । यथार्थ में ई बाघ सब नव-नव स्थान पर नहिं गेल अछि; अपन ऐतिहासिक आवास मे वापस आबि रहल छथि। प्रकृतिविद ई.पी. गी, 20म शताब्दीक प्रारंभ मे पूरा भारत मे लगभग एक लाख बाघ छल । तहिया सं ओहि इलाका मे सं बहुत रास इलाका मे मानव बस्ती, कृषि, आ बुनियादी ढांचा विकास के कब्जा भ गेल अछि.

मानव जनसंख्या के दबाव के तीव्रता के उदाहरण बांधवगढ़-संजय दुबरी क्षेत्र स भेटैत अछि | 1901 मे एहि इलाका मे प्रति वर्ग किलोमीटर मात्र 9 लोक रहैत छलाह, जखन कि आब 223 लोक एहि इलाका मे रहैत छथि। एहन स्थिति मे बाघ आ मनुक्खक बीच मुठभेड़ आ टकराव बढ़ब स्वाभाविक अछि ।

बाघ मे बहुत लंबा दूरी तय करबाक क्षमता होइत छैक । जनवरी २०२४ म॑ राजस्थान केरऽ सरिस्का टाइगर रिजर्व स॑ लगभग १२५ किलोमीटर दूर दिल्ली महानगर के पास एगो बाघ कृषि भूमि प॑ पहुँची गेलऽ छेलै । हालांकि यात्रा के दौरान दू लोग घायल होय गेलै, लेकिन रेडियो कॉलर के आंकड़ा स॑ एकरऽ गंतव्य वापस सरिस्का के तरफ होय के पुष्टि होय के कारण वन अधिकारी न॑ हस्तक्षेप नै करलकै । विशेषज्ञ क अनुसार भविष्य मे एहन घटना बढ़बाक संभावना अछि।

सड़क विकास एवं संरक्षण हाथ मे हाथ मिला

वन क्षेत्रक कें टुकड़ा-टुकड़ा करय वाला सड़कक कें सही योजना बनावा पर वन्यजीव संरक्षण कें लेल सेहो औजार बनि सकय छै. भारत केरऽ वन्यजीव संस्थान केरऽ वैज्ञानिक बिलाल हबीब के अनुसार सड़क निर्माण क॑ रोकी नै सकै छै, लेकिन एकरा वन्यजीव के अनुकूल बनालऽ जाब॑ सकै छै । ओ कहलनि, 'हम सभ खाली सड़क नहि बना रहल छी; हम परिदृश्य आ पारिस्थितिकी संपर्क कें बहाल कयर रहल छी. हम सभ भूमि प्रकृति मे वापस क' रहल छी।'

हुनकऽ अनुसार भारत केरऽ विभिन्न राज्यऽ न॑ बाघ आरू हाथी केरऽ सीमा पार के आवाजाही क॑ ध्यान म॑ रखतें हुअ॑ समन्वय बढ़ाबै के काम शुरू करी देल॑ छै । वन्यजीवक कें लेल अंडरपास, ओवरपास, आ सुरक्षित गलियाराक कें निर्माण कें विकास योजनाक कें अभिन्न अंग बनावा कें प्रयास कैल जा रहल छै.

विश्वप्रसिद्ध बाघ विशेषज्ञ उल्लास करंथ सेहो एहि बात पर जोर दैत छथि । हुनकऽ शब्दऽ म॑ ‘कोर आवासऽ के सबसें पहलें रक्षा करना जरूरी छै । अगर आवास के नीक सं संरक्षण कएल जाए त भारत 10 सं 20 हजार बाघ के सेहो सहारा द सकैत अछि.' हुनकर अनुसार अंडरपास आ ओवरपास मात्र पर्याप्त नहि अछि। बाघ एकर उपयोग तखने करत जखन एहि संरचना सभक दुनू कात गुणवत्तापूर्ण जंगल होयत ।

ई अनुभव नेपालक लेल सेहो अत्यंत प्रासंगिक अछि । जेना-जेना चितवन, पर्सा, बर्दिया, बांके, आ शुक्लफंटा मे बाघक आबादी बढ़ैत गेल अछि, चुनौती आब बाघक संख्या बढ़ेबाक नहि, बल्कि जैविक गलियाराक रक्षा करबाक अछि जतय ओ सुरक्षित रूप सँ घुमि सकैत अछि । पूर्व-पश्चिम राजमार्ग, प्रस्तावित रेलवे, आ अन्य बुनियादी ढांचा परियोजना मे वन्यजीव अंडरपास, ओवरपास, आ हरित गलियारा कें अनिवार्य रूप सं शामिल करला सं ही नेपाल दीर्घकाल मे अपन संरक्षण सफलता कें कायम राखि सकय छै.

नेपाल आब लेल पाठ

नेपाल बाघक जनसंख्या बढबैत संरक्षणक सफल उदाहरण विश्वक समक्ष प्रस्तुत केलक अछि । मुदा आब चुनौती बाघ के गिनती नहिं, बल्कि एहन माहौल बनाबय के अछि जतय ओ सुरक्षित रहय. चितवन, पर्सा, बाँके, बर्दिया, आ शुक्लफंटा के बीच वन्यजीव गलियारा के सुरक्षा, पूर्व-पश्चिम राजमार्ग, रेलवे, आ अन्य बुनियादी ढांचा पर वन्यजीव के अंडरपास आ ओवरपास अनिवार्य करब, आ नेपाल-भारत सीमा क्षेत्र में संयुक्त संरक्षण रणनीति अपनाबय के काज समय के जरूरत अछि.

सचमुच नेपालक बाघक जनसंख्या मे वृद्धिक परिणाम पूर्णतः सकारात्मक नहि अछि । सरकारी अभिलेख अनुसार नेपालमे २०१९ सँ २०२४ धरि बाघ आक्रमणक कारण ४४ गोटेक मृत्यु भेल अछि । एहि हमला मे शामिल 15 टा बाघ कए पकड़ि कए अस्थायी बचाव आ होल्डिंग सेंटर मे राखल गेल अछि। जाहिमे बर्दियामे पाँचटा बाघ, चितवनमे चारिटा, काठमाण्डौके केन्द्रीय चिड़ियाघरमे चारिटा, पर्सा आ शुक्लफन्तमे एक-एकटा बाघ राखल गेल अछि ।

बाघ के संख्या में वृद्धि संरक्षण के सफलता अछि। मुदा, जं जंगल आ सुरक्षित मार्ग जतय ओ स्वतंत्र रूप सं घुमि सकैत छथि, ओकर रक्षा नहिं हो तं ओ सफलता दीर्घकालीन नहिं भ सकैत अछि. यही कारण छै कि अब॑ बाघ के ही नै बल्कि ओकरऽ चलै वाला रास्ता के भी रक्षा करना जरूरी छै, आरू बाघऽ स॑ हाशिया प॑ पड़लऽ समुदाय क॑ सुरक्षित रखना जरूरी छै । ई चुनौती आसान नहि अछि।
